reason: The cited evidence does not directly address the key premises. E1 discusses enhanced Cr enrichment in passivation films of ultrafine-grained stainless steels, not the effect of bulk chromium content on film continuity or corrosion rate. E2 describes oxide layer oxygen penetration in specific alloys but does not compare high- vs. low-chromium steels or confirm Cr2O3 as a diffusion barrier. The premises lack specific prior evidence support.
premises: High-chromium steels form a continuous, protective Cr2O3 film
This Cr2O3 film acts as a diffusion barrier limiting oxygen and corrosive species ingress
Low-chromium steels form less protective or discontinuous oxides
The Cr2O3 film reduces the overall corrosion rate compared to low-chromium steels
Selective oxidation of chromium leads to rapid formation of the protective layer
